Task14.intro: For Task 14 (P2CG1 and activation), replacing or adding to the P2CF1 list:

corrected.wording: On every change of the component's binding, dispose the previous consumer before the new bind. The host fold is reset to `EMPTY_CAMPAIGN_AUTHORITATIVE_FOLD` per binding; the guest mirror is module-scoped and is NOT reset: a receipt baseline replaces it from EMPTY (`applySnapshot(event, -1, true, facts)`), a legacy join keeps quoting its `lastSequence`. A rebind does not imply a reconnect: `connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport` reuses the match's active transport (see CF11).

A baseline offer is adopted with `replacement = true` and the frame's bundle at cursor -1: `foldCampaignHydration(fold, frame.event, frame.hydrationFacts, true, -1)` for the host, `applySnapshot(frame.event, -1, true, frame.hydrationFacts)` for the guest, so a first live event at sequence 0 is admitted. The receipt chain, not the cursor, orders offers.

unchanged.wording: **CF7, CF8, CF9**: unchanged from the P2CF1 review and the P2CF1 closure receipt.

hardPreconditions.concern: M1 precondition (closure lives in the P2CF1 transport leaf)
hardPreconditions.wording: Before `applicationReceipts` is composed into `bindCampaignSyncConnection` and `expectedCampaignId` is bound at every creator (CampaignCoopEntryPanel.tsx 328, CampaignCoopRouteSurfaceConnected.tsx 156 and 268, launch.tsx), close M1 by one of: (a) the client ignores `campaign-application-unknown-receipt` when a newer offer has been registered since the refused ACK (`latest !== sent`) and otherwise rejoins; (b) the binder admits an ACK of any established receipt of the live view as `stale` (no frame) and reserves `unknown-receipt` for receipts the view never issued, or names the refused `appliedView` in the refusal frame. Record the choice in the owning unit's contract before source execution.
hardPreconditions.placement: The author's placement is right. `handleApplicationRefusal` in the P2CF1 transport calls `recover('application-refused')` (view torn down, `failed = true`, `pending` cleared) before any `onError` listener runs, so the consumer cannot "ignore a superseded unknown-receipt"; option (a) can only live in `campaignSyncTransport.ts`, a P2CF1 leaf outside `restrictions.P2CF2`. Editing it would have been an unregistered leaf. CF7 stands as the Task 14 precondition.

also.wording: Decide the client bound for head-drift re-sends (m1) and for a lost refusal (P2CE3 Task14 item 4): either route typed refusals through `sendConfirmed` or have the consumer rejoin after a bounded wait without confirmation or refusal.

`connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport` returns `null` when an existing transport's `campaignId` differs from the supplied `expectedCampaignId`; bind at every creator in the same change, or the mounted surface detaches from the entry panel's transport.

new.wording: The consumer's rejoin closes the match's shared transport and deletes it from `activeTransports`. `CampaignCoopEntryPanel.tsx` (328-344) and `launch.tsx` (149, 177) hold references to the closed instance and never learn of the replacement. Before `expectedCampaignId` is bound at those creators, either make them resolve the transport through `getActiveCampaignSyncTransport` on each use, or publish a registry change the surface's rejoin triggers, or make the mounted surface the sole creator of the bound transport.

A host binding on an already-hydrated bound transport (route navigation between the three host-mounting pages, a StrictMode remount, any effect re-run without the transport closing) starts from EMPTY with `latched = false`; its first linked offer fails the adjunct check and forces a rejoin. Before activation decide one of: hold the host fold in a module-scoped store like the guest mirror so a rebind continues the lineage; close the transport in the surface cleanup so every binding gets its own hydration; or accept one rejoin per navigation and measure it. Keep `retainsLaunchFacts` in every case: with it removed the rebind ACKs a fold seeded from EMPTY as applied (reviewer probe P1).

`socket.onclose` sets `closed` and clears `pending` but emits nothing; a close with no offer in flight is invisible to the consumer (probe P7). When the transport leaf is next open, surface the close (an `onClose` handler or an `emitError` with a recovery-required reason) and make the consumer rejoin on it.

In `useCampaignApplicationConsumer.ts`, chain `.catch(() => rejoin())` on the per-offer queue step so a throwing `confirmApplied` (or any future throw outside `settle`'s try) ends the binding with a rejoin instead of stalling the queue (probe P4).

`adoptFlushedRevision` adopts a row without bumping `loadGeneration`; a guarded refresh whose GET read the pre-flush row can install an older `baseVersion` after it. Bump the generation in `adoptFlushedRevision`, or refuse to adopt in the guarded path when `migrated.version < get().baseVersion`.

Task14.testsToRegister: **Tests to register with the next change that opens these leaves:** the host sequence-0 case (m7), P1 as a registered case and a GM fact-bearing baseline/launch case (m8).

majorM2.finding: **M2 (new; design-level, Task 14 cost, not a P2CF2 deviation). Rebind on a live transport starts from EMPTY.** `connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport` returns the match's active transport when one exists (lines 495-505); the surface's cleanup never closes it; the host fold is a `useRef` of this component and is now reset on every effect run. So every binding that is not the first on a connection (route navigation between `CampaignDashboardPage.tsx` 354, `personnel.tsx` 107 and `campaignPageShell.tsx` 358, a StrictMode remount, a `roomCode`-only change) binds an EMPTY fold with `latched = false` to an already-hydrated connection that will send no new baseline. In receipt mode the next linked offer fails the adjunct check and forces a rejoin (P1): correct state, one reconnect per navigation. In legacy mode the next event seeds the fold from empty (pre-existing for a fresh mount; new for a `roomCode`-only change, which no client code performs today: `coopSession.roomCode` is written only at creation in `CampaignCoopEntryPanel.tsx` 258/333). The registered proof ("starts every host binding from an empty fold...") installs a mock `connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport` that records a new connect per call, so it demonstrates the reset but not production's reuse. My CF1 wording ("before the new transport opens") assumed a reconnect per rebind; I correct it in section 9. Owner decision before Task 14 activation (CF11): hold the host fold in a module-scoped store as the guest mirror is, or close the transport in the surface cleanup so each binding gets its own hydration, or accept one rejoin per navigation; in every case keep the adjunct check, which is what makes the path fail closed.
majorM2.verdictSummary: One new major (M2) that is a design-level cost for Task 14, not a defect in this slice: the host fold is component-local and resets per binding, while `connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport` reuses the match's live transport, so any rebind without a reconnect (route navigation between the three host-mounting pages, a StrictMode remount, a `roomCode` change) starts a binding from EMPTY on an already-hydrated connection. In receipt mode that costs one rejoin per occurrence (fail-closed through the adjunct check, which my probe shows is load-bearing there, so the author's "H15 equivalent" claim is wrong); in legacy mode it is the pre-existing lossy seed. The test that proves the per-binding reset uses a mock that opens a new connection on every call, so it does not model the real transport's reuse.
majorM2.probeP1: | P1 host rebind on a live, already-hydrated bound transport (dispose A, reset fold, bind B, inject linked r2) | no ACK for r2, socket closed, one rejoin: fail-closed via `adjunct-failed` (`launchFacts` undefined on the from-empty fold). **With the adjunct check removed (H15) the same probe ACKs r2 as `applied` over a fold seeded from EMPTY** (balance 700_000, chain r0 r1 r2, no rejoin). H15 is not equivalent. |
majorM2.cf1Correction: My CF1 wording ("before the new transport opens") assumed a reconnect per rebind; I correct it in section 9.

recoverySemantics: "One rejoin per occurrence": `rejoin()` is idempotent per binding (`live` flag), closes the transport, and bumps `rejoins` so both effects re-run; the host resets its fold, the guest's next baseline replaces. Each M1 hit therefore costs one close + fresh join + replacement baseline; durable state is unaffected (cumulative commit already covers the refused receipt). Safe but not free; the frequency at Task 14 is why CF7 is hard.
Unlimited rejoins: each cycle needs a server refusal or close, so there is no tight loop; a server that refuses every join would cause a reconnect per refusal. CF8 (bounds) stands.

Rejoin closes the shared transport: `transport.close()` deletes it from `activeTransports`; the entry panel and the launch page keep references to the closed instance. Unreachable before Task 14 binds creators; new carry-forward CF10.

`confirmApplied` throwing stops the queue without a rejoin (author concern 1): confirmed by probe P4 (baseline confirm throws -> no ACK, no refresh for the next offer, `rejoins` 0, jest reports the rejection). Nothing in the shipped transport throws there (send failures are caught inside `drain`), so fail-closed today; m9.

Socket close with no offer in flight: confirmed invisible (probe P7, `rejoins` 0 after `onclose`). The transport's `onclose` sets `closed` and clears `pending` but emits nothing; the consumer learns only through a `refused: closed` confirm result or an INTERNAL_ERROR frame. Transport leaf; CF12.

P2CF1 minors status.** m1 (re-send bound) -> CF8 stands. m2/m3 (transport untested branches) remain; the transport was correctly not touched. m4 (byte equality on non-replacement hydration) is closed for the client: the consumer never uses the non-replacement path for a baseline. m5 (fold does not check the snapshot's campaign on non-replacement) is covered three times on the receipt path: the consumer gate, `registerOffer` (`frame.event.campaignId !== options.expectedCampaignId` -> prefix-conflict, P5) and `projectAuthoritativeStateOntoCampaign` (`current.id !== campaignId` -> null -> `projection-failed`). m6 (dropped confirmation) is moot: the consumer awaits no confirmation (CF4 honoured).

deviationsJudged.cursorMinusOne: Cursor -1 versus CF3's literal 0 (author deviation): correct. The server frames every baseline at `sequence: -1` (`bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts` 1859, `CampaignSyncSession.ts` 932) and the log hands out sequences from 0 (`campaignHostBatchCommit.ts` 112 `sequence = await host.nextSequence()`, healed logs start at `nextSequence: 0`; the mirror store's own doc says "the following log events (sequence 0+)"). `foldCampaignEvent` refuses `event.sequence <= fold.lastSequence`, so a baseline adopted at 0 would refuse a first live event at 0 and the consumer would report `fold-rejected`, which the transport turns into `recover('application-failed')` and a rejoin loop on a fresh campaign. The legacy adopt-at-0 convention (`foldCampaignFrame`, entry panel `applySnapshot(snapshot, 0)`) carries that latent edge; the receipt path avoids it. The ordering guarantee on the receipt path comes from `registerOffer`'s receipt chain (`previousReceiptId === latest.receiptId`), not from the cursor, so -1 loses nothing. The guest side is pinned; the host side is not (m7).
deviationsJudged.guestMirrorNotResetPerBinding: Guest mirror not reset per binding (author deviation from CF1): correct, and better than my CF1 wording. The mirror store is module-scoped and holds the lineage across a rebind (probe P8: a second binding on the same live transport continues the chain and ACKs r2 with the right date and balance); `beginMirror` per binding would discard the entry panel's seeded mirror and the `lastSeq` the legacy guest join quotes; in receipt mode every baseline is an authorized replacement from EMPTY, which is the "reconnect cannot adopt stale held proof" clause at the mirror level. CF1 is corrected in section 9.
deviationsJudged.N1: **N1.** Deviations judged: cursor -1 (section 2) and the guest mirror not reset per binding (section 3) are both correct and should become the behaviour text at closure: "the baseline is adopted as an authorized replacement from EMPTY at cursor -1; the guest mirror is replaced by the view's baseline rather than reset per binding; a guarded refresh does not announce `saving`".

notes.wording: **N1.** Deviations judged: cursor -1 (section 2) and the guest mirror not reset per binding (section 3) are both correct and should become the behaviour text at closure: "the baseline is adopted as an authorized replacement from EMPTY at cursor -1; the guest mirror is replaced by the view's baseline rather than reset per binding; a guarded refresh does not announce `saving`".

**N2.** `consume` on an inactive binding returns `isOffer(message)`, so an offered frame on a transport bound to another campaign is neither folded nor ACKed and the transport leaves it `prefix-pending`. Fail-closed by design; the behaviour text's "foreign application ... gives no receipt" covers it.

**N3.** The three receipts are internally consistent with the ledger and with `report.md`/`census.md`; the red receipt's two-round story (first-text REDs, probe round one 38/45, lint-units fix, final 34 failed / 28 passed / 62) is plausible and I did not re-run RED (the base product bytes are in the admission receipt and the final test text is on the head; the mechanism is the same as P2CF1's, which I reproduced).

**N4.** `report.md` concern 3 ("a stale guarded refresh does not re-arm autosave is harmless because a co-op GM's `markDirty` never arms") is true for `markDirty` (`isCoopCampaign` returns early) but an armed timer can also come from the ordinary refresh's own re-arm or from flush reconciliation. The contract chose "once invalidated it does not re-arm"; conformant, and the stale paths (unmount, rejoin, later load, reset) each have their own successor write. No change needed.

**N5.** P9: on a bound transport before any offer has latched `receiptMode`, an unoffered `CampaignEvent` is still folded by the legacy path and still earns a numeric observation ACK from the transport. Only a server that sends an unoffered frame on a bound connection before the baseline could produce it; the Task 14 binder sends the baseline first. Documentary.
